summary.name: Futuristic UI (FUI) / HUD Design is a supplemental style in the Digital and 3D Aesthetics category. Its note describes a descriptive futuristic-interface direction, and not every cyberpunk scene is a HUD.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit cues call for dark backgrounds, fine wireframes, limited cyan or magenta accents, and readable monospaced data. Panels, reticles, scales, maps, and progress rings must each have a defined function. Overexposed neon and meaningless microtext are avoided.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: fictional interfaces and title sequences, plus hybrid use when the HUD must show meaningful data or signal readouts that drive visible events. Inferred: operations dashboards, mission-control style reports, and diagnostic or sensor sequences in tech trailers. Motion-017, 037, 038, and 039 list this style as a compatible fit.
summary.limitations: Explicit: do not add off-palette accents, and do not use magenta alongside cyan unless the topic and interface palette support both. Avoid excessive spinning rings and decorative rings without a data role. Keep bloom selective, keep waveforms inside panels, and label all fictional data. Simulated HUD appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics.
summary.palette: Palette is an optional, style-compatible suggestion used only when no approved palette is supplied. Tokens are background #0C1822, foreground #E7F4F3, and accent_1 #55C7CF, with no gradient. Under chroma-js 3.2.0, foreground on background measures 15.933 and dark text on the cyan accent measures 8.942. These are two-color checks only, so composited frames must be rechecked. Task-supplied exact colors override these suggestions.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Motion should tie startup, scanning, acquisition, and feedback to visible data events, so every readout change has a visible cause. Use smooth authored movement with readable holds, and keep sharp cuts where the action needs them. Live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belong only to interactive delivery; video must be driven by seekable composition time. Optional references are motion-017 for separable components, and motion-037, 038, and 039 only when inspected assets support them.
summary.audio: No fixed audio direction is specified, and the audio choice is optional and topic-driven. Explicit style-linked suggestion: seeded cyan waveform traces that lock to acquisition events, with subtle glow, can pair with sound. Music, voiceover, and effects are not mandated. Do not invent audio assets, honor user audio requirements first, and verify speech intelligibility and sync in the final video.
summary.assetRequirements: Needed assets include a readable monospaced font, which is unspecified, and local font files loaded before capture. Fictional or authorized data must be supplied or generated and labeled. Approved mark geometry or glyph assets are required for the phrase, punctuation, and burst motions. Leaflet maps require authorized geographic data and tiles, with attribution.
summary.combinations: Explicit: style-097 pairs with HUD data panels, using accurate D3 or Leaflet charts and maps with cyan for active values. Explicit: style-063 pairs with seeded oscilloscope-style waveform traces inside bounded panels. Both combinations bar off-palette accents and decorative rings. Hybrids are advised when the HUD must display meaningful data, and pure FUI works alone for fictional interfaces.
summary.productionApproach: Style renderer: SVG and Three.js handle wireframes, point-line 3D forms, scales, and text, with UnrealBloomPass only for selected luminous elements. Motion engine: one paused, seekable GSAP timeline with one owner per property; Motion is optional and needs explicit synchronization. Pipeline: HyperFrames is primary, validated with check, snapshot, and render; Remotion is a fallback only when a recorded limitation applies. Verify forward, backward, and direct seeks.
